cards.front: One word (adjective) for: eating both plants and flesh
reasons: review:Correct and unambiguous, but inconsistent: sibling herbivorous/carnivorous cards are good while this is must. Make it good.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: One word for: unable to pay one's debts (the adjective that describes the person)
cards.note: Insolvent (adj.) describes a person or firm whose debts exceed what it can pay.
reasons: review:Meaning correct, but "bankrupt" is an equally standard adjective answer for unable to pay debts; the front does not exclude it. Add a cue such as "debts exceed assets" or note bankrupt as legal declaration, or drop.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: He decided to ____ from his homeland, India, to settle in Canada. (emigrate / immigrate)
cards.note: 'Emigrate' = leave one's own country (emigrate from). 'Immigrate' = enter a new country to live (immigrate to). Here the cue is leaving his homeland.
reasons: review:"from his homeland ... to settle in Canada" still fits "immigrate from India to Canada" (valid usage); cue is not decisive. Reword to focus on one side, e.g. "He decided to ____ from India" with no destination.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: when a past reporting verb reports a past event or state, what happens to the tense (unless it is a universal truth)?
cards.back:
It moves one step back (present becomes past). A universal truth keeps the present tense.
Wrong: He said that he is tired (when he was tired then).
Right: He said that he was tired.
cards.note: Exception: "He said that the earth moves round the sun." stays present.
reasons: review:Imprecise: front says past event or state but back says present becomes past; a past event goes simple past to past perfect (had + V3). Rephrase back to cover both steps, and universal truth exception also covers habitual facts.

cards.subject: english
cards.back: Excessively eager to please or obey
reasons: review:Note lists antonym arrogant; the true opposite of servile/fawning is assertive or domineering, arrogant is only loosely opposed. Meaning itself is right; fix the note antonym.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: in reported speech after a past reporting verb ('said that'), how does the tense change?
cards.back:
It moves one step back: am/is becomes was, has/have becomes had, and the simple past becomes the past perfect.
Wrong: She said that she has submitted the form.
Right: She said that she had submitted the form.
reasons: review:Rule is stated as always true but is only generally true: omits are->were, will->would, can->could, and present tense stays for universal truths or still-valid facts. Add these or narrow the front.
